issues.legal_issue: An interlocutory mandatory injunction restoring possession in a commercial contract dispute cannot be granted without applying the governing equitable tests and addressing material contrary findings and whether damages are adequate.
material_facts: A commercial dealership agreement allowed the corporation to revoke the arrangement for breach, and the dealer had changed the structure of the firm without obtaining prior permission.

The corporation terminated the agreement and claimed it had taken possession and handed the outlet to another entity; the dealer disputed when possession was taken and claimed to have been dispossessed later.
The trial court considered documents concerning possession, found that the dealer had not shown a strong prima facie case, and denied interim relief, including restoration of possession.

The High Court granted interim relief after treating the termination as prima facie illegal and finding that the dealer was in possession when the suit was filed, but it did not address the trial court’s reasons or whether damages could adequately compensate the dealer.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order granting interim relief was unsustainable and was set aside; the trial court’s refusal of interim relief was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Interlocutory injunctions require consideration of a prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury. A mandatory interlocutory injunction is subject to stricter guidance: the applicant should have a strong case for trial, relief should be necessary to prevent irreparable or serious injury not normally compensable in money, and the balance of convenience should favour the applicant. The court must weigh the competing risks of injustice (Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co.; Dorab Cawasji Warden v. Coomi Sorab Warden). In a commercial distributorship dispute, compensation rather than restoration may be the appropriate remedy where the agreement is revocable (Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. Amritsar Gas Service).

rule.if: interlocutory_mandatory_injunction_appeal and trial_court_rejected_relief_after_assessing_the_record and (possession_is_seriously_disputed or damages_may_compensate_for_the_injury) and appellate_court_granted_restorative_relief_without_assessing_irreparable_harm

predicates.interlocutory_mandatory_injunction_appea: The proceeding is an appeal concerning mandatory interim relief sought during a pending suit.
predicates.trial_court_rejected_relief_after_assess: The trial court considered the material on record and refused the requested interim relief.
predicates.possession_is_seriously_disputed: The parties give materially conflicting accounts of who possessed the property and when possession changed.
predicates.damages_may_compensate_for_the_injury: The alleged injury may be adequately compensated by damages rather than requiring interim restoration.
predicates.appellate_court_granted_restorative_reli: The appellate court ordered interim restoration or comparable mandatory relief without addressing whether refusal would cause irreparable harm.

issues.definition: When an appellate court grants restorative mandatory interim relief despite an assessed refusal by the trial court and serious disputes or potentially adequate monetary compensation, its order is set aside if it has not assessed irreparable harm.

issues.legal_issue: At the interlocutory-injunction stage, a contested contractual termination must be examined only to the extent needed to assess a prima facie case, while unresolved questions about its validity are left for trial.
material_facts: The dealer had changed the structure of the firm without prior permission, and the corporation relied on the agreement in terminating the dealership.
The parties disputed whether the corporation was required to allow the dealer an opportunity to rectify the alleged breach and whether termination without that opportunity was invalid.
The High Court addressed the termination’s validity in detail when deciding the interim applications, although those questions remained contested and were to be resolved in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The validity of the termination was not finally determined; it could be considered at the interim stage only for the limited purpose of assessing whether a prima facie case existed, with the contested questions left for the hearing of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: An interlocutory injunction is considered while the asserted right and its alleged violation remain uncertain pending determination on evidence at trial. The court may assess the challenged act only so far as needed to decide whether a prima facie case exists; it should not determine contested contractual questions in detail at the interim stage. The ordinary interlocutory-injunction principles discussed in Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co. apply.

predicates.interlocutory_injunction_stage: The court is deciding a request for interim relief while the underlying suit remains pending.
predicates.contractual_termination_is_contested: One party challenges the termination of a commercial agreement and the other party relies on it.
predicates.termination_validity_depends_on_unresolv: The parties dispute contractual duties or procedures whose application has not yet been resolved at trial.

issues.definition: When interim relief is sought and the validity of a contested contractual termination depends on unresolved contractual questions, the court assesses that validity only provisionally for interim relief.
